problem: End-to-end navigation models still depend on spatial information (depth, poses, goal localization) supplied by external SLAM or pretrained 3D reconstruction modules, so state estimation and navigation are optimized separately and navigation objectives cannot shape how the world state is learned and maintained.
motivation: World models must process streaming observations, keep memory, predict futures and update state, which mirrors SLAM's incremental updates with persistent memory and backend refinement. Bringing these mechanisms inside the navigation model lets geometric and navigation objectives jointly shape a shared world state and lets inference continuously correct drift.
key_idea: Unify a video-generation expert (dreaming goal-conditioned futures) and a SLAM expert (depth+pose, also acting as inverse dynamics on dreamed frames) in one autoregressive Mixture-of-Transformers with persistent KV cache and a local backend refinement, trained jointly for navigation and SLAM.
insight: The shared SLAM expert localizes observed frames and does inverse dynamics on dreamed frames in the same metric coordinates, keeping plans anchored to a goal fixed in the first-camera frame: replacing it with a plain IDM (no depth/localization) drops SR by about 36 points (28.1 vs 64.6 Home). The local backend refining recent states adds a further +2.0/+1.3 SR, and reward-based post-training of only the generation expert adds ~5.5 SR, showing that better dreamed futures matter as well.
method: Unified MoT: three experts (RGB generation, depth, pose; depth+pose form the SLAM expert) with own parameters and joint self-attention across 30 layers; initialized from Wan2.2-5B, depth/pose experts by interpolating weights to widths 1536/768

Dream + SLAM formulation: generation expert dreams goal-conditioned future RGB latents; the same SLAM expert estimates states for observed frames and, as inverse dynamics, for dreamed frames, giving the metric plan (16 poses per planning step)

Teacher-forcing training with attention mask: clean RGB/state tokens are causal context, noisy RGB tokens and state queries attend to earlier chunks, no leakage; loss = flow matching + depth MSE on VAE latents + smooth-L1 abs/rel pose losses
Local backend: re-estimates depth/poses of the latest k frames in the current chunk as new frames arrive, updating states and KV cache to reduce accumulated drift
Persistent KV cache closed-loop inference: controller tracks a pose prefix, observed frames appended, generated frames discarded, cache up to 128 latent frames, 8 sampling steps at 320x192

Safety-prioritized RL post-training: DiffusionNFT on self-attention LoRA of the generation expert only (SLAM expert frozen), reward = safety-gated softmax of progress-matching cost versus expert trajectory, evaluated using occupancy maps without a simulator

setting.backbone: Wan2.2-5B-initialized Mixture-of-Transformers (generation + depth + pose experts), fine-tuned
setting.training_data: InternVLA-N1 (InternVLN-N1) navigation dataset, 95% for training (5% held out for SLAM test); pretraining 10 epochs, post-training ~10% hard trajectories for 1 epoch; 48 A100 GPUs
setting.observation: monocular RGB only (320x192); depth and pose estimated by own SLAM expert
setting.action_space: predicted camera pose trajectory (16 poses/step, executes to 4th pose) tracked by a low-level controller
setting.privileged: Goal position in first-camera frame given; no external odometry or depth at test time. Post-training uses dataset occupancy maps and expert trajectories.

numbers.extra: RGB only; 20 Home scenes x 100 episodes; success within 1 m
RGB only; 20 Commercial scenes x 100 episodes; success within 1 m

numbers.eval_set_note: 5% held-out InternVLN-N1 trajectories (all RGB trajectories in that split)
numbers.extra: 320x192 input; trained on InternVLN-N1 only; Sim(3) alignment

numbers_note: Post-training ablation given only in a figure (SR +5.7/+5.4, SPL +4.8/+4.9 on Home/Commercial in text). Navigation benchmark split is disjoint from training; labelled test.
results: With RGB only, WSM reaches SR/SPL 70.3/66.3 (Home) and 73.9/71.8 (Commercial), beating LoGoPlanner (re-evaluated 59.6/53.6 and 65.8/62.0, which uses RGB-D) by 10.7 and 8.1 SR points. It also gets ATE 0.021 m vs 0.041 m for fine-tuned SLAM-Former, but worse dense accuracy (0.062 vs 0.041 m).
limitations: Depth is encoded in the appearance-oriented Wan2.2 VAE latent space, hurting geometric fidelity (worse Acc. RMSE than SLAM-Former)
Uncompressed history KV cache makes memory and compute grow with frames, limiting long-horizon deployment
Evaluated only in simulation on one start-goal benchmark; no real robot experiments
